Added scope from the user (2026-11-20): "Ultimately, it might be good to take dxf drawing, create model in sc and generate cc project for it."

6. **Drawing to project.** A 2D DXF drawing goes to a SolidCraft model (DXF into a sketch, extrude the outline to the stock thickness, cut the inner profiles to their depths), then to a CamCraft project (stock from the model, a setup, the operations chosen per feature). Questions:
   - Which parts of this already work through the two MCP servers, and what is missing on each side? CamCraft has DXF sketches (#1862) with 2D ops on them (#1864, #1867-#1870); SolidCraft has a DXF insert.
   - How are depths given when a DXF has none? Options: per layer, by a name convention, a short form, or asking.
   - When should a job go via SolidCraft? A model is needed for 3D ops and simulation. For a flat part, CamCraft's own DXF route may be enough.
   - Is the first step a skill or agent workflow driving both MCP servers, before anything is built into either app?

Clarification from the user (2026-11-20): the input is mostly **DWG** drawings: "drawing -> model / cad -> cam".

7. **DWG input.** DWG is a closed binary format. Options to research:
   - (a) an external converter to DXF, run as a separate program, never linked: LibreDWG's `dwg2dxf` (GPLv3) or the free ODA File Converter. Licences and DWG version coverage (R2018+) need checking.
   - (b) a native DWG reader. Probably not worth it: large, and it raises licensing and provenance questions.
   - (c) ask users to save as DXF from their CAD.
   Recommend one. Note anything in a converter's licence that limits shipping it or calling it from CamCraft or SolidCraft.

8. **Drawing kind.**
   - A single profile plus a thickness (a plate) maps straight to sketch, extrude and cuts.
   - A dimensioned multi-view engineering drawing (front/top/side, sections) needs interpretation: matching the views and reading the dimensions and notes. An agent could do this for prismatic parts with the solidcraft-modeling approach (numbers first, then build and measure). Full automatic reconstruction from views is research-grade.
   Which drawings do real users have, and what share of them is the simple kind?

Note for questions 6-8: SolidCraft 0.45.0 (2026-11-19) added **drawings**, in the model-to-drawing direction. It places base, projected, section and flat-pattern views, adds dimensions, notes and parts lists, exports a sheet as SVG or PNG, and has MCP commands (`drawing.view.base`, `drawing.view.projected`, `drawing.check`, ...). It does not read a drawing back into a model, and it exports no DXF or DWG.

Two uses here:
- **A test oracle for drawing-to-model.** Build a known part in SolidCraft, make its dimensioned drawing, then have the agent rebuild the part from the drawing alone and compare the result with the original. An exact STEP comparison gives a measured success rate per drawing kind, which answers question 8 with data.
- **A shop drawing next to the CAM output.** A dimensioned drawing could go with CamCraft's setup sheet.

## Findings: conversational (no-model) operations, Q1-Q8

Research only, no code. Vendor material was used only as a checklist of *which* operations shops expect. No wording, labels, parameter names or screen flows were taken. Inputs below are in plain machining terms. No Autodesk, Fusion or HSMWorks material was read.

Codebase facts were read on `upstream/main` (2026-11-20). The one that matters most: **a 2D operation whose source is a placed DXF profile is refused at generation on main.** `sketch_model::generation_problem` says "a toolpath from the chains of a DXF profile is not generated yet". #1862 shipped placement only; #1864 and #1867-#1870 are still open. Every "front end" row below waits on those issues.

### Q1 + Q2: common operations, who has them, what CamCraft has

Legend for the CamCraft column:
- **covered**: works today with no model.
- **front end**: the operation kind and generator exist, but they need geometry the user types as numbers, plus profile generation from #1864/#1867-#1870.
- **new**: real toolpath or geometry work.

System keys: PP = PathPilot, Hu = Hurco WinMax, Hd = Heidenhain cycles, Si = Siemens ShopMill/ShopTurn, Mz = Mazatrol, Ha = Haas VPS/IPS, FM = Fanuc Manual Guide i, Ce = Centroid Intercon, LC = LinuxCNC NGCGUI library, Ki = Kipware. A blank means I did not confirm it, not that the system lacks it.

**Mill**

| Operation | Systems | Inputs (machining terms) | CamCraft today |
|---|---|---|---|
| Face to size | PP, Hu, Hd (233), Si, Mz, Ha | XY extent (or the stock), top Z, final Z, depth per pass, stepover, direction | **covered**: Face with source = stock |
| Hole pattern: list, line, grid | PP, Hu, Hd (220/221), Si, Mz, Ce, LC | XY points, or start + pitch + count (+ angle); R plane, depth, cycle (spot, drill, peck, dwell, tap, ream, bore), peck step, dwell, tap pitch; optional spot tool | **front end**: Drill has every cycle (`CycleChoice`) but finds holes in a model. Needs point/circle sketch geometry and Drill on sketch circles |
| Bolt-hole circle (full or partial) | PP, Hu, Hd (220), Si, Mz, Ce, Ki, LC | centre XY, circle diameter, hole count, start angle, angular pitch or arc span, plus the drilling inputs above | **front end** (same as above) |
| Rectangular / circular pocket | PP, Hu, Hd (251/252), Si, Ce, Ki, LC | centre or corner, length × width or diameter, corner radius, depth, stepdown, stepover, entry (ramp/helix/plunge), finish allowance | **front end**: Pocket, Adaptive2D, Circular exist; generation on profiles is #1867 |
| Rectangular / circular boss, outside frame | PP, Hu, Hd (256/257), Si, Ce | boss size, corner radius, stock size around it, depth, stepdown, stepover | **front end**: Contour/Pocket, #1864/#1867 |
| Polygon / special pocket (hex, triangle) | Hu, LC | across-flats or corner diameter, side count, rotation, depth | **front end** (one more sketch shape) |
| Straight slot / keyway (end mill) | Hd (253), Si, LC-type wizards | start, end (or centre, length, angle), width, depth, stepdown | **front end**: Slot, TrochoidalSlot, #1868 |
| Arc slot | Hd (254), Si | centre, radius, start angle, span, width, depth | **front end** (#1868) |
| Keyseat with side-entry cutter (Woodruff, T-slot) | wizards; handbook practice | cutter diameter and width, slot depth, axial position | **new**: side-entry plunge geometry, gouge check on the arbor |
| Thread mill, internal / external | PP, Hu, Hd (262-267), Si | centre, major diameter, pitch or TPI, hand, length, radial passes | **front end**: Thread exists on model holes (#992 rule: the hole must be drilled first) |
| Helical bore / circle to size | Hu, Si | centre, diameter, depth, pitch per turn | **front end**: Bore exists |
| Engrave text | PP, Hu, Si, Hd | text, start point, height, angle, depth | **almost covered**: `insert_text` (#2679) places the strokes; generation is #1869 |
| Chamfer an edge | Si, Hu | the profile, chamfer size, tool angle | **front end**: Chamfer2D exists |
| Contour typed as lines/arcs | Hu, Ce, Si, Hd | segments in order, with a solver for tangent and intersection points | **new**: a sketch-authoring tool |
| DXF straight to a cut | PP, Ki | file, offset, scale, rotation, side per shape, cut order | **in progress**: #1862 shipped, #1864/#1867-#1870 open |
| Repeat, pattern or mirror an operation | Hu, Ce, Si | offset, rotation or mirror axis, count | **new**: no operation patterning today |

**Lathe**

| Operation | Systems | Inputs | CamCraft today |
|---|---|---|---|
| Face | PP, Si, FM, Ha, Ki | start diameter, end diameter (0 or a bore), Z to face to, depth per pass | **front end**: Facing exists but turning kinds need a revolved model |
| OD/ID turn: diameters, lengths, tapers, chamfers, radii | PP, Si, FM, Mz, Ha, Ki | a table of steps (diameter, length, corner type and size), stock diameter, rough depth, finish allowance | **new geometry source + front end**: ProfileRough/Finish, TaperTurning, Chamfering and BoringTurning exist, but there is no turned half-profile from numbers. Profiles are admitted for the 2D, plasma and wire kinds only |
| Groove: OD, ID, face | PP, Si, FM, Ki | position, width, depth or floor diameter, corner breaks, count/pitch | **front end**: GrooveRough/Finish |
| Thread: OD/ID, straight | PP, Si, FM, Ki | major diameter, pitch or TPI, length, hand, infeed, spring passes, relief | **front end**: Threading, already posted as G76 on Fanuc-family posts |
| Thread relief / undercut | Si | relief standard or width, depth, radius | **front end** once the profile source exists (it is profile geometry) |
| Part-off | PP, Si, Ki | Z position, final diameter, chamfer, peck | **front end**: Part |
| Centre drill, drill, tap on axis | PP, Si, Ha, Ki | diameter, depth, peck, tap pitch | **front end** |

A count from these sources: hole patterns (bolt circle included), rectangular/circular pockets, facing, and thread milling or threading appear in every system I could confirm. Bosses/frames, slots and engraving appear in most.

### Q3: where it lives

**Recommendation: a quick operation, not a wizard.** One undoable command that does both of these as one History step:
- creates a sketch profile from a parametric recipe (rectangle with corner radius, circle, obround slot, polygon, point list, linear/grid/circular pattern; for lathe, a turned step table),
- creates a normal operation on that profile.

It ships with an MCP tool (`add_quick_op`, or one per shape family). The recipe is stored on the sketch, so editing the numbers later is an undoable `EditSketchRecipe` that regenerates the chains. The operation stays an ordinary operation: same parameter page, same verify, same post.

Why not a separate wizard:
- A wizard would duplicate the parameter pages.
- It would bypass "Everything Is a Command" unless it compiled down to commands anyway.
- It would make a second kind of operation the simulator and the gouge verdict would have to learn.

The UI part is a small form in the Stock/Sketch area that issues this command. Users who want guidance get it from the form; nothing else changes.

This reuses the profile machinery from #1862 and #1864-#1870 instead of adding a parallel geometry path. It also means a DXF profile, typed text and a typed bolt circle are all the same kind of thing.

### Q4: output style

**The expanded, simulated toolpath stays the source of truth. The post folds it into a canned cycle only where the fold provably gives the same motion.**
- **Drilling already does this** (G81/G82/G83/G73/G84/G85/G86/G89 per post) and should stay the default for hole patterns. That is what conversational users expect and read.
- **Cutter compensation:** default quick-op contours, bosses, frames and pocket finish passes to the existing `Compensation::Wear` (G41/G42 with the cutter-centre path; the register holds only wear). The program stays exact if the offset register is zero, and the operator can still trim size at the control. The lead and open-chain refusal laws already exist.
- **Lathe threading:** G76 already exists on Fanuc-family posts. Keep it.
- **Not recommended for now:**
  - control-side pocket, boss and roughing cycles (G12/G13, Heidenhain 25x, Siemens POCKET, lathe G71/G70),
  - subprogram-per-depth.

  With these, the control computes motion the simulator never verified. That runs against "never gouge". Revisit them as post options only with a golden equality test between the cycle's documented motion and our expansion. (Tormach's own post guide also says PathPilot does not support G70-G73 roughing cycles.)

### Q5: proposed sub-issues, in order

Prerequisites already filed: #1864, #1867, #1868, #1869 (they make profile-based operations generate). Several items below are blocked by them.

| # | Title | P | effort | area |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | Quick ops: hole patterns from numbers (point list, line, grid, full/partial bolt circle), with Drill/Tap/Ream/Bore/Thread on sketch points and circles | P6 | high | 2d, mcp |
| 3 | Quick ops: face to size on a stock-only setup (form + MCP over the existing Face) | P6 | high | 2d, mcp |
| 4 | Quick ops: pockets, bosses/frames, slots/keyways and arc slots on recipe sketches (needs 1, #1864/#1867/#1868) | P6 | high | 2d |
| 5 | Quick ops default to wear-mode cutter compensation where the post supports it (Q4) | P6 | high | 2d, post |
| 6 | Agent skill: DXF/DWG drawing to SolidCraft model to CamCraft project through both MCP servers (Q6) | P6 | medium | mcp |
| 7 | Lathe: turned half-profile sketch from a step table (diameter, length, chamfer/radius, taper) as a turning source | P8 | max | turning |
| 8 | Lathe quick ops on that profile: face, turn, groove, thread with relief, part-off, axial drill (needs 7) | P8 | high | turning, mcp |
| 9 | Typed contour: lines and arcs entered as numbers, with tangent/intersection solving, into a sketch | P8 | max | 2d |
| 10 | Pattern, repeat and mirror an operation (offset, polar, mirror) | P8 | max | 2d |
| 11 | Side-entry keyseat (Woodruff, T-slot cutter) operation | P8 | max | 2d |

Every row that produces or changes posted G-code is effort:high or more (safety floor). Row 6 is a skill. Row 12 runs a separate program; any DXF it produces goes through the existing reader.

On text engraving: once #1869 lands, `insert_text` plus Engrave may already be the quick op. No new issue unless a check after #1869 shows a gap.

### Q6: DXF drawing → SolidCraft model → CamCraft project

**Works today:**
- **SolidCraft:** `sketch.insert_dxf` (path or text, offset, scale, join tolerance, plane) puts the drawing in a sketch. `solid.extrude` makes the plate and the cuts. `file.export` writes the model. In my local checkout of SolidCraft (2026-10-26), its DXF reader:
  - **drops layers**,
  - **reads a file with no units as mm.** That is a silent guess; CamCraft's `import_dxf` refuses such a file until units are given.
  
  Open SolidCraft DXF import reports include #7509, #2300, #10875, #11644, #14685 and #19131.
- **CamCraft:** the model route is complete: import STEP, set stock, setup, operations on picked features or holes, simulate, verify, post. `import_dxf` and `insert_text` place profiles, but profile operations do not generate yet (#1864/#1867-#1870).

**Missing:**
- **SolidCraft side:** layer names carried into the sketch (so depths can be mapped by layer), and a units question or refusal instead of assuming mm.
- **CamCraft side:** generation on profiles; a depth per chain or per layer on 2D operations; and (optional, later) a feature-to-operation suggestion for an imported plate (through holes → Drill, closed inner loops → Pocket, outer → Contour).

**Depths when the DXF has none.** In order of preference:
1. **Ask once, with a table**: each layer and closed-chain group with its count and size range, the user answers depth or "through".
2. A layer-name convention, accepted only when it parses exactly, and echoed back for confirmation.
3. Never guess.

In CamCraft this becomes one operation per depth group, with its bottom height set.

**When to go through SolidCraft:**
- the job needs a solid: 3D operations, a gouge verdict against the finished part, rest material, edge chamfers/fillets, more than one setup (flip), fixtures in sim;
- or the user wants the model anyway.

**When the CamCraft DXF route is enough:** a flat single-setup plate with through cuts and pockets (once #1864 and the others land). It has fewer conversions and keeps arcs exact. Note that the profile route checks against the stock and the chains, not against a solid.

**First step:** yes, an agent skill that drives both MCP servers (row 6), before anything is built into either app. It costs no app code and exercises both MCP surfaces end to end. Each gap it hits becomes a precise issue in the right repo. Build into the apps only the steps the skill shows are repetitive.

SolidCraft 0.45.0 (2026-11-19) added model → dimensioned drawing with `drawing.*` MCP commands. This is the reverse direction, so use it as a **round-trip oracle**:
1. Draw a known model.
2. Have the skill rebuild a model from that drawing.
3. Compare the two with SolidCraft's exact STEP comparison (volume, bounding box, hole positions).

This gives the skill a test suite with no hand-made fixtures.

### Q7: DWG input

| Option | Licence (from the vendor's own pages) | Versions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a1) LibreDWG `dwg2dxf` | GPLv3 or later | Reader handles all DWG versions, R2018 and R2024 included; some advanced R2010+ objects are skipped; dwg2dxf claimed "about 90%" coverage; project still beta | Running it as a separate program the user installed creates no GPL obligation for CamCraft or SolidCraft. Bundling the binary in our installers means shipping it under GPL with its source offer: possible, but a maintainer decision |
| (a2) ODA File Converter | Free, but ODA's FAQ limits non-members to **non-commercial use only**. ODA says it does not distribute it to third parties; only the latest version is public | DWG/DXF across versions (ODA's SDK datasheet: through AutoCAD 2025, AC1032) | Has a CLI (source dir, target dir, filter, output version, audit). **Cannot be bundled.** A shop using it commercially needs ODA membership. Do not make it the default |
| (b) Native reader | — | — | Large, a moving format, and a provenance risk. Not worth it |
| (c) Save as DXF in the user's CAD | none | whatever the CAD writes | Always works, zero risk. Every CAD that writes DWG also writes DXF |

**Recommendation:**
- **(c) is the documented default.**
- **(a1) is the optional convenience**: if `dwg2dxf` is on PATH, offer to convert. Run it as an external program with a timeout. Feed its output through our existing DXF reader with its fuzz-tested refusals, and show the import summary so skipped entities are visible.
- Do not bundle either converter now.
- Do not use ODA by default; at most mention it in docs with its non-commercial terms stated.
- Converter output is untrusted input like any DXF.

### Q8: drawing kind

- **Profile plus thickness (plates, brackets, panels, sign blanks): feasible now.** Sketch → extrude → cuts in SolidCraft, or the CamCraft profile route. This is the WorkBee/router crowd's typical job.
- **Dimensioned multi-view drawings: feasible for prismatic parts only, agent-assisted, never automatic.** The agent reads the views and dimensions into a numbers list and builds the model by the solidcraft-modeling method (numbers first, then build and measure). It confirms with the user anything a view leaves ambiguous: hidden lines, sections, tolerances, notes. The 0.45.0 round-trip oracle above makes this measurable. Full automatic 3D reconstruction from views is research-grade; out of scope.
- **What share is simple:** no data. Proposal: ask the machine-owner contacts and Discord for 10-20 real drawings (DXF or DWG) and sort them into plate / prismatic multi-view / other. Pick the skill's first targets from that count, not from a guess.
